title: Hybrid Retrieval Beats Pure Vector on Domain-Specific Corpora

sections.abstract: We compare BM25, vector, and hybrid retrieval on three corpora.
sections.methods: Three corpora; four embedding models; reciprocal rank fusion.
sections.results: Hybrid retrieval (BM25+vector via RRF) outperformed pure vector by 8-14 hit-rate points on the technical corpora and was within 1 point on the general-knowledge corpus.
sections.discussion: Hybrid wins where exact-string matches matter (codes, names, identifiers). On general-knowledge corpora the gap closes.

title: Reranking as the Single Largest Quality Lift in Production RAG

sections.abstract: We study the effect of cross-encoder reranking on real workloads.
sections.methods: Five production RAG pipelines; A/B testing with and without reranking.
sections.results: Adding a cross-encoder reranker improved final-answer quality by 20-35% across the five pipelines, measured by human-graded rubrics.
sections.discussion: Reranking helps because retrieval scores are coarse. Joint query-chunk scoring catches relevance signal that vector or BM25 alone misses.

title: Chunking Strategies for Long Technical Documents

sections.abstract: We evaluate four chunking strategies on a technical-docs corpus.
sections.results: Section-aware chunks outperformed fixed-size by ~12 points on hit rate. Contextual prefixes added another 4-6 points on top of section-aware.
sections.discussion: Document structure carries information that vector embeddings alone do not capture; chunkers that respect structure perform better.

title: Eval Set Curation: A Practitioner Survey

sections.abstract: Survey of how teams build and maintain LLM eval sets.
sections.results: Teams that maintained eval sets > 30 entries, updated weekly, and gated releases on regression checks shipped fewer high-severity incidents.
sections.discussion: Eval discipline correlates with shipping confidence. Teams that skipped eval sets reported repeated regressions and faith-based deploys.

title: Tool-Use Stability in Long Agent Loops

sections.abstract: We analyze tool-call success rates as a function of agent loop depth.
sections.methods: Synthetic and production traces; 4 frontier models; 14 tool families.
sections.results: Success rate degrades sharply past 8 tool-call rounds. Most production failures cluster between rounds 9 and 14.
sections.discussion: Bounding the loop is a cheaper reliability win than fine-tuning. Hard caps + explicit re-planning beats deeper context windows.

title: Citation Validation Reduces Hallucination in Long-Form Synthesis

sections.abstract: We study post-generation citation validators as a hallucination defense.
sections.methods: Compare three RAG pipelines with and without validators that check every cited source exists in the indexed corpus.
sections.results: Citation validators caught 12-19% of generated outputs as having at least one unverifiable citation, which would have shipped to users without the check.
sections.discussion: Cite-first prompting alone is not sufficient; output-side validation is needed because models occasionally fabricate plausible-looking IDs.
